html:
Vat Phou is a ruined temple complex at the foot of a mountain near Champasak in southern Laos. It was a sacred site from about the 5th century, and most of its standing buildings date from the 11th to 13th centuries, under the Khmer Empire.

The mountain above it has a natural peak shaped like a linga, so it was holy to the Hindu god Shiva. A road ran from Vat Phou to Angkor, and the site was linked with early kingdoms before Angkor rose.

Later it became a Buddhist shrine and is still the scene of a yearly festival. It was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2001. Compare Angkor Wat and Hinduism in the region.
